propositions: Review gate criterion runners return untyped values that cannot distinguish clean execution from failed, cancelled, skipped, shed, or resumed outcomes, causing plan-review failures to become empty successful checkpoints and code-review to lose earlier work when later criteria raise.

A new independent discovery submodule must define immutable typed plan/result schemas with six outcome kinds (success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, cancelled) and a dependency-aware synchronous executor that schedules units, accumulates usage, observes cancellation, and creates checkpoint envelopes only for success/resumed results.

Budget shedding is deterministic and minimal, proceeding in ascending dependency-rank and unit-id order with cascade-skipping of unmet dependents, stopping once the kept set fits the cap, and identical across runs; zero and uncapped omission are both valid, disabling never happens silently.

The versioned digest-complete envelope identity covers material, code/ref, effective-policy, prompt, contract, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and schema version constant, round-tripping only content-identical success/resumed units while failed, cancelled, skipped, and shed units remain missing.

Systemic config/provider-init failures and cancellation abort remaining work with exact completed-so-far accounting; an already-dispatched non-interruptible call commits as its true success/failed outcome with real usage, while a not-yet-dispatched unit is cancelled.

The stored trace is normalized diagnostic metadata and lineage only, excluding raw prompts, ticket/context bodies, provider responses, and secrets, and does not change existing review result schemas or add per-unit traces to review/review-status contracts.
